Temporary Changes to Referral and Authorization Processes Ending November 30, 2026

Oct 06, 2026

Beginning December 1, 2026, the Department will require members to complete a Single Assessment within the past 12 months before processing referrals, prior authorization requests, and continued stay reviews for children’s medium- and high-intensity services. 

As previously communicated, the Department temporarily reinstated direct-to-provider referral and prior authorization processes while operational challenges with the Single Assessment process were being addressed. That temporary process will end November 30, 2026. 

The Single Assessment process has stabilized significantly, with assessments now completed in an average of 7.5 business days after a request is submitted. 

Thank you for your continued partnership with the Single Assessment process.

Board of Occupational Safety and Health to Host Listening Sessions on Proposed Indoor Air Quality Compliance Directive

October 6, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Board of Occupational Safety and Health (BOSH) and the Maine Department of Labor Bureau of Labor Standards (BLS) Workplace Safety and Health Division invite interested parties and the public to participate in listening sessions on a proposed voluntary compliance directive on indoor air quality.

BOSH regulates and enforces workplace safety and health rules that apply to public employers, including state and local governmental agencies, school districts and quasi-governmental agencies. BOSH is considering publishing a voluntary compliance directive to help public employers monitor and maintain healthy indoor air quality in public workplaces. The proposed compliance directive is based in part on the research and recommendations of the Indoor Air Quality Advisory Group in 2025.

BOSH and BLS will host the following listening sessions:

New MaineCare Partner Portal: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements

Oct 06, 2026

As a reminder, the new MaineCare Partner Portal is scheduled to go live on October 12, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The new portal will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal and will require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Read below for more information and steps you will need to take to sign into the MaineCare Partner Portal starting on October 12. 

For all information about the upcoming changes to MIHMS, see the “HealthPAS Online Portal” section of the Provider Resources page.  

Multi-Factor Authenticator (MFA) 

MFA adds a second verification step after entering your password. This is an important new security measure to protect the sensitive information held in the Portal. You will have three options to choose from for your additional authentication factor; you must choose one.

Follow the instructions below for first-time setup of the option you choose. 

  1. Microsoft Authenticator 

The Microsoft Authenticator app is the recommended MFA method because it offers the highest level of protection over other methods. Download the Microsoft Authenticator app now on a smartphone or tablet so that you are ready to use it on October 12. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via the app:  

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Open the Microsoft Authenticator app. 
  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Click the QR code scanner in the Microsoft Authenticator app and scan the QR code displayed on the Portal’s User Details window.  

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Text/Call 

Text (SMS) or call verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027.  

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via text (SMS) or call: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Text/call” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter a phone number, request a code or call, then verify the code. The phone number you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Email 

Email verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via email: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Email” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter an email address, request a code, then verify the code. The email address you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process. 

 

For additional instructions on both initial setup and ongoing use of MFA, including screenshots, please reference the job aid MaineCare Partner Portal MFA Setup and Access Job Aid. 

  • You can find this job aid and other supporting resources through the MMIS Learning Center. Search for the course “ME – MIHMS Upgrade Documentation,” enroll in the course, then look for the job aid in the documentation list. 
  • Starting October 12, 2026, this job aid will also be available in the MaineCare Partner Portal under the Provider tab > Provider Manuals subtab. 

Need Help? 

If you have questions about these instructions, please call Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. 

Thank you for preparing in advance for a smooth transition to the new MaineCare Partner Portal.

Changes Coming to Call Center Phone Menus

Oct 07, 2026

Starting on October 12, 2026, when the MIHMS upgrade goes live, we are also changing how callers interact with and experience Provider Services and Member Services call center phone menus, known as Interactive Voice Response (IVR). With the goal of increasing caller satisfaction, these changes will provide a modernized IVR experience with streamlined navigation, clearer call flows, and improved overall caller efficiency.    

Intelligent Contact Center - Gabby 

  • A virtual assistant, called Gabby, will replace traditional phone menus by listening to what callers say to resolve simple inquiries. 
  • When unable to resolve an inquiry, Gabby will pass the call reason and context to a live agent. 
  • Gabby can answer common provider questions 24/7, with information such as: 
    • Verifying member eligibility 
    • More ways to search for claims information 
    • More detailed provider enrollment status 
    • Providing the five most recent payments 
    • Prior authorization information 
    • Library of FAQs to assist callers with common questions

entry.title: US Department of Labor cites Pennsylvania excavation employer for failing to provide trench protection following fatal trench cave-in
entry.content: CHAMBERSBURG, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an excavation contractor for willful and serious safety violations after a young worker was fatally injured in a trench collapse. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration opened an investigation into Jonas David Wagoner – doing business as J.D. Wagoner Excavating – on April 2, 2026, and found workers were installing a storm sewer system 12 feet below ground level in a trench that was not adequately protected from soil collapse. When a portion of the trench's wall failed, the unrestrained soil engulfed one worker. The agency issued a willful violation for failure to protect workers from cave-ins and two repeat violations for failing to assign a competent person to conduct daily trench inspections and removing employees from hazardous conditions.In addition, the employer received three serious violations for failure to provide construction hazard prevention training to employees, establish a safe means for workers to exit the excavation site, keep materials at least two feet from the edge of an excavation site, and restrain side materials from becoming roll-in hazards. OSHA proposed $254,884 in penalties. The employer has 15 business days from receiving receipt of its citations and penalties to request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

MaineCare in Education: Updated Joint Individual Education Program (IEP) Guidance for School Health-Related Services

Oct 08, 2026

As a reminder, all providers who deliver services following the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) must ensure all MaineCare-covered services are documented following the Department of Health and Human Services/Maine Department of Education Joint IEP Guidance document. 

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

DOE first released the Joint Guidance on August 28, 2026, and has re-issued this guidance effective September 18, 2026. The reissued guidance replaces the previously issued Joint Guidance and provides clarification in response to questions and feedback received from School Administrative Units (SAUs), providers, and other interested parties. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. 

Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. Acentra will accept IEP language from both versions through October 18, 2026. Beginning October 19, 2026, Acentra will only accept IEP language from the new version re-issued on September 18, 2026. 

For technical assistance regarding the billing and processing of MaineCare claims, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist. 

For all other questions related to the provision of MaineCare School Health-Related Services, please contact Trista Collins, State Medicaid Educational Liaison.    

For technical information related to IEP development, please contact Dan Hemdal at the Maine Department of Education.

entry.title: Saving Money on Winter Heating Costs
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Well, it's getting more and more painful to fill up at a gas station or fill a tank of oil to heat your home. And we all know why.

Look, we're making progress shifting to other sources of energy to heat our homes, but we're still the most dependent on heating oil to heat our homes in the in the entire country. That reliance on heating oil makes us vulnerable to great shifts in global energy markets that drive up costs for Maine people and businesses. This president's war in Iran right now has created the largest fuel supply disruption in global history and has driven energy prices to record highs. The price of heating oil in Maine has reached more than $6 a gallon, so you'll be paying almost $800 more to fill a standard 275 gallon tank than you did a year ago. Kerosene prices are also reaching historic highs, all because of this war.

Maine people should not be forced to choose between staying warm or putting food on the table because the president chose to drag us into a needless war -- and an endless war, it appears.

My administration is doing what it can to help people save money on heating costs and stay comfortable in their homes this winter.

It's not enough, but I've directed the Department of Health and Human Services to identify households that would be eligible for $40 million in discounts on their electric bills through Maine's Low Income Assistance Program, or LIAP. Starting in November, thousands of eligible families who are customers of CMP or Versant will begin to see discounts ranging from 20 percent to 80 percent, and these will be applied automatically every month to their electric bills. It's one thing we can do. Families who already get federal assistance for home heating oil through LIHEAP, the Low Income Energy Assistance Program, will also be enrolled automatically in this state assistance program, LIAP, to get the maximum savings on their electric bills without any unnecessary paperwork. Customers with questions about this discount should contact their electric company directly.

I've also called on Congress to increase funding for federal home heating assistance, and I thank Maine's congressional delegation for their bipartisan support for LIHEAP funding, despite the president's attempts to eliminate this program. And that's just not enough, though, to make up for the skyrocketing costs driven by tariffs and the president's war. Congress must ensure the safety and comfort of Maine people heading into this winter season by increasing LIHEAP funding.

In the meantime, MaineHousing has distributed about $4 million to heating fuel companies for some of our most vulnerable households, those with older adults on small incomes or small children. Those trucks will begin delivering fuel to those homes over the next few days. We're also talking to farmers and foresters and other entities that use diesel fuel a lot about other ways we might be able to help them address high diesel prices here in Maine.

I'm proud to say that thanks to our investments over the years in energy efficiency and clean energy, our reliance on heating oil has fallen from 70 percent of Maine households in 2010 to just over 50 percent now. Still, it's not enough. My administration will continue to make it as affordable as possible to transition to clean energy sources like heat pumps, to save people money, and to make sure we're not left to shoulder the burden of the president's blunders.

Are you interested in exploring heat pumps or using wood or propane to heat your home instead of oil and kerosene? Are you curious about energy assistance programs? Weatherization? Do you need contact information for local community action agencies or MaineHousing or Efficiency Maine Trust? Our Winter Heating Guide, published every year by the Maine Department of Energy Resources, has all that information, as well as some helpful tips about winterizing and saving money, and about contact information, and links to online resources. You can view and download that Winter Heating Guide and review the latest heating fuel prices at Maine.gov/Energy.

This crisis affects all of us – low income, middle income, everyone who has a home, everyone who has a bill to pay this winter. But as the weather continues to get colder, I encourage all Maine people to see how they might save money and stay warm through the winter by using our current Maine Winter heating guide found at Maine.gov/Energy.

This is Governor Janet Mills. Please stay warm, and thank you for listening.

MaineCare Coverage of Gender-Affirming Care for Medicaid Beneficiaries Under Age 18 and Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Enrollees Under Age 19

Oct 09, 2026

As described in the message sent September 18, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published a final rule in the Federal Register on August 13, 2026, that limits federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for certain gender-affirming care provided to minors. This rule prohibits federal matching funds for puberty blockers, cross-sex hormone therapy, and surgical interventions when used for gender transition for Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. The federal rule is scheduled to take effect on October 13, 2026. 

The federal rule does not prohibit states from using state-only funds to cover these services. Maine law requires MaineCare to cover medically necessary treatment for or related to gender dysphoria and protects members from discrimination based on gender identity or gender expression.   

To ensure we are in compliance with this new federal rule, we have established the billing requirements below for providers who deliver gender-affirming care services to Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. 

Effective on October 13, 2026, medical claims submitted through the MIHMS system must: 

  • Include applicable gender-affirming care diagnosis codes on all claims. 
  • Include the SE modifier on any claims submitted for gender-affirming care, other than behavioral health services.  
    • The SE modifier is used to identify a service that must be reimbursed using state-only funds.  
    • The SE modifier should be listed after any other modifiers on the applicable claim line(s). 
    • Behavioral health treatment for gender dysphoria is still eligible for federal match, so providers are not required to include the SE modifier on behavioral health-related claims.  

Effective on October 9, 2026, pharmacy claims submitted through the MEPOPS system must:  

  • Have Prior Authorization (PA) as required on the Department’s Preferred Drug List. This requirement applies to preferred and non-preferred products on the Department’s identified medication list.   
  • Include the medication’s intended clinical use by including the applicable diagnosis code and the information needed to determine the appropriate coverage and funding pathway.  
    • Medication prescribed for a clinical use outside the scope of 42 CFR § 441.801–441.802 and 457.476 remains subject to the otherwise applicable MaineCare pharmacy criteria. For medication prescribed for use within the scope of those provisions, the Department will review coverage under its separately funded state-only benefit.  

This PA requirement is used to determine clinical purpose and payment source. It does not, by itself, change the drug’s preferred status, establish additional step therapy, or mean that all uses of the medication are excluded from federally matched coverage. Existing drug-specific clinical criteria continue to apply as appropriate.  

For questions, please contact Provider Relations Specialist, Lisa Bouchard.

System Remittance Advice (RA) and 835 Limitations

Oct 13, 2026

Attention Nursing Homes, Hospitals, and Private Non-Medical Institutions, Appendix C & F (PNMI-C-F): Claims RA/835 Issues

Following the MIHMS upgrade, there are open issues affecting some RA/835s.  The issues are high priority for a fix that is underway; we are currently targeting to fix the issues by the end of October and will send another communication when the issues have been resolved. This message provides details of the issues and available workarounds until the issues are fixed. 

Cost of Care Reporting for Nursing Home, Hospital Claims, and PNMI-C-F 

Nursing Home and Hospital claims for members with cost of care are not being reported with the appropriate Claim Adjustment Reason Code (CARC) needed for balance billing members. 

  • PDF RA – CARC 142 is not being reported for cost of care. 
  • 835 – CARC 96 is being reported in error. 

As a workaround until the fix is in place, MaineCare will provide a report that can be accessed on the MaineCare Partner Portal. On the Dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Cost of Care Report.” This report will be available on Mondays for the claims finalized on the prior Wednesday. Because this week’s claims will be finalized on Thursday, the first report will be available no later than Tuesday, October 20, 2026.  

Spenddown Reporting for Provider Claims 

Claims with spenddown are not being reported with the appropriate CARC needed for balance billing members. 

  • PDF RA – CARC 142 is not being reported for spenddown claims.   
  • 835 – CARC 96 and/or CARC 178 is being reported in error. 

As a workaround until the fix is in place, MaineCare will provide a report that can be accessed on the MaineCare Partner Portal. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Spend Down Report.” This report will be available on Mondays for the claims finalized on the prior Wednesday. Because this week’s claims will be finalized on Thursday, the first report will be available no later than Tuesday, October 20, 2026.  

Hospital Crossover Claims 

Hospital crossover claims are not reporting the correct CARC when the member has Medicare and full MaineCare coverage, and the claim balance is for deductible or coinsurance.  In this situation, you would normally expect a B1 CARC. 

  • PDF RA – CARC B1 is being reported appropriately. 
  • 835 – CARC 45 is being reported in error. 

As a one-time workaround, MaineCare will provide a report after this issue has been resolved. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Bad Debt Write off Report.” We anticipate this report will be available by November 13, 2026, and will confirm once the issue is resolved. 

Claims Processed in Excess of Charges 

Claims processed in excess of billed charges are not being reported with the appropriate CARC. 

  • PDF RA – Reporting CARC 94 appropriately. 
  • 835 – Claims that pay more than the billed amount (i.e. FQHC, Hospitals with APC, DRGs) are reporting CARC 45 instead of CARC 94. 

MaineCare does not have a workaround for this issue, as CARC 45 and CARC 94 share the same Claim Adjustment Group Code of CO (Contractual Obligation). MaineCare can provide a report upon request; please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.  

For questions, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585.

entry.content:
WHEREAS, blindness and low vision affect millions of Americans, including an estimated 35,000 Maine people; and 

WHEREAS, the white cane and guide dog serve as essential tools that promote independence, mobility, and safety for people who are blind or have low vision, and Maine law recognizes their use and provides protections for people who use them; and 

WHEREAS, people who are blind and or low vision contribute significantly to the social, cultural, and economic vitality of our state as they pursue meaningful careers in diverse professions, strengthen Maine's workforce, raise families, and enrich our communities through their participation in all aspects of life; and 

WHEREAS, we honor the resilience, wisdom, and lifelong contributions of older adults who are blind or have low vision, and their efforts to maintain independence while navigating the unique challenges of aging with vision loss; and 

WHEREAS, people with vision loss continue to encounter stigma, discrimination, and accessibility barriers, including misconceptions about their capabilities and needs; and 

WHEREAS, we recognize the efforts of vision rehabilitation professionals, educators, self-advocates, and allies across Maine who work to advance equality, accessibility and opportunities for people who are blind or have low vision; and 

WHEREAS, Blindness Awareness Month calls attention to the importance of accessibility, inclusion, and respect, and reminds us of the progress achieved through advocacy, education, and civil rights protections, as well as the work still to be done; 

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 2026 as 

Blindness Awareness Month

in Maine, and I call upon all residents to join in recognizing the contributions of Maine people who are blind or have low vision and to work together to promote accessibility, inclusion, independence, and full participation in all aspects of community life.

The MaineCare Third Party Liability (TPL) Exemption Request and Attestation Form is Now Available

Oct 13, 2026

On August 3, 2026, MaineCare announced claims system updates to support proper TPL reimbursement processes in accordance with MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Chapter I, Section 1.07 TPL rules. The MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form is now available for TPL exemption request submission.  

Requesting TPL Exemption 

In accordance with MBM, Chapter I, Section 1.07 rules, MaineCare may assess the validity of extenuating circumstance or service code TPL exemption requests to bill MaineCare as the primary payer for services delivered to a member with primary, public, or commercial coverage. Providers wishing to apply for TPL exemption to bill MaineCare as the primary payer must complete and submit the MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form to the TPL Medicare Code Exempt Request email box.  

MaineCare will review completed forms with the supporting documentation and provide a decision letter of approval or non-approval via email to the requestor. An exemption request approval letter is valid only for a specific member for a defined duration, no greater than 12 months. The exemption request approval letter must be attached to all applicable MaineCare claims for dates of service during the approved time. Claims without a valid and up-to-date approval letter may result in denials.  

Providers are responsible for maintaining exemption request renewals by submitting a subsequent MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form at least 30 calendar days prior to the expiration date specified in the approval letter.  

Limited Retroactive TPL Exemption Review Period 

For a limited time, MaineCare will consider continuity of care retroactive exemption requests with supporting documentation for claims directly impacted by the system updates announced in the Provider Responsibility Regarding Third Party Liability and Secondary Billing e-message we sent on August 3, 2026.  

After December 31, 2026, retroactive exemption requests may not be accepted for review. Providers who receive retroactive exemption request approvals may resubmit their claims with the applicable approval letter attached for claims processing. 

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

entry.title: US Labor Department finds 6 New York, New Jersey construction employers exposed workers to safety hazards, assesses combined $648K in penalties
entry.content: MONROE, NY – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited six construction employers for willful and serious safety violations involving excavation hazards at the site of a planned 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building and proposed a combined $648,094 in penalties. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to an allegation of struck-by and collapse hazards associated with a large excavation at the Monroe Commons project – also known as Magna Square development – a planned 4-story, approximately 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building with retail, office space, and a 39-room hotel located on an 18-acre site. The excavation had a steep, unstable embankment nearly 75 feet high which was not adequately sloped or shored. OSHA issued a total of 23 serious and five willful citations to the project’s general contractor and five subcontractors for failing to protect employees from cave-in, struck-by, and chemical hazards; neglecting to shield employees from falling or rolling rock and soil from an excavation face; and not ensuring daily inspections of excavations were conducted by a competent person. Advanced Plan and Build LLC, and subcontractors Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. – operating as Drip Drop Waterproofing Inc. – and The Paving Masters LLC received citations for willfully exposing employees to cave-in and struck-by hazards from an unprotected excavation. OSHA also cited Advanced Plan and Build and The Paving Masters for their willful failure to ensure that the excavation, which was between 21 and 75 feet deep, was designed by a registered professional engineer. Subcontractors Century Max Industries Corp., DelValle Contractor, and Prime Structure Inc. were cited for serious violations for failing to protect employees from cave-in and struck-by hazards. DelValle and Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. also received citations for serious violations related to lack of fall protection and chemical hazards.OSHA proposed the following penalties: Advanced Plan and Build LLC—$175,444; Century Max Industries Corp.—$46,340; DelValle Contractor—$19,151; Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc.—$198,615; Prime Structure Inc.—$19,860; and The Paving Masters LLC—$188,684. The employers have 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

Title IV PostsecondaryInstitutions: Workforce Pell Program Applications Open for Second Review Cycle Through Nov. 13

October 14, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist | media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA -The State Workforce Development Board(SWDB) is accepting applications from Title IV postsecondary institutionsseeking stateapproval to offer programs eligible for federal Workforce Pell Grants. Applications for the second review cycle are due Friday, Nov. 13

Maine's Workforce Pell application provides an online process for eligible postsecondary institutions to seek approval to offer short-term workforce training programs that meet federal Workforce Pell Grant requirements. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly by the SWDB.

Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage and in-demand careers. States are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before they are submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state,"said Vaughan Woodruff, chair of the State Workforce Development Board."The program's support for training that connects people with skills needed for Maine's workforce presents a significant opportunity for Maine workers and employers."

The Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy establishesthe state's process foridentifying, reviewing and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. The policy was developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System and University of MaineSystem.

"Workforce Pell brings a new source of federal funding to Maine's short-term workforce training programs," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "We are excited to help Maine's postsecondary institutions take advantage of this opportunity to strengthen their programs, reach more students and prepare Maine's workforce for the future."

The SWDB will evaluate applications and make recommendations to the Governor for state certification. Programs certified by the Governor will then be submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval. Following federal approval, the SWDB will publish the list of Maine-certified Workforce Pell programs on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage within 30 days.

Institutions can find the Workforce Pell application, eligibility requirements, program guidance and additional information on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage.

  • Payments

These programs will focus on high-growth and emerging industry sectors such as skilled trades and construction, healthcare, information technology, manufacturing, domestic energy production, and business and professional services. entry.title: US departments of Labor, Health and Human Services expand efforts to help employees access health benefits
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The departments of Labor and Health and Human Services announced that representatives from several large employers with self-insured health plans signed a statement of support for the expansion of electronic prior authorization reform to the self-insured markets. “The departments appreciate these U.S. companies for stepping forward to collaborate with Labor and Health and Human Services to help employees cut through red tape and receive their health benefits,” said Assistant Secretary for Employee Benefits Security Daniel Aronowitz. “By signing this statement of support for the expansion of electronic prior authorization reform, government and private industry are working together on behalf of the American workforce.”Signed by five delegates from Amazon, Axon Enterprise Inc., Google, Meta, and Oracle Corp., the statement supports the June 2025 Prior Authorization Pledge, which contains six key reforms, including standardizing all prior authorization submissions, reducing the volume of medical procedures that require preapproval, and making sure medical professionals review all clinical denials. It also asks third party administrators to enhance transparency and communication around authorization decisions and appeals.“Patients and doctors shouldn’t have to fall back on faxes and paperwork simply because of how a patient’s health plan is funded,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “We’ve brought insurers, providers, and technology companies to the table to modernize prior authorization, and now employers are helping us take another important step. When the entire healthcare system moves together, we can spend less time on paperwork and more time getting patients the care they need.”Over the past year, the Trump Administration and industry partners have implemented electronic prior authorization reforms. In 2025, leading insurance companies signed the Prior Authorization Pledge to improve the process for their Medicare Advantage, Medicaid Managed Care, Health Insurance Marketplace, and commercial plans. Read the employer statement of support.

entry.title: US Department of Labor cites Illinois utility construction company for repeated exposure to trenching hazards
entry.content: CHICAGO – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Frankfort-based utility construction company for repeatedly exposing employees to excavation safety hazards after federal investigators observed employees working in an unprotected trench.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration initiated an investigation of Always Underground LLC as part of its National Emphasis Program on Trenching after witnessing employees working in an unprotected trench deeper than eight feet.OSHA cited the employer for three repeat violations for failing to provide workers with a safe means of egress, to install a trench protective system that would protect against cave-ins, and to keep excavated or other materials and equipment at least 2 feet from the edge. Additionally, the agency cited the employer for a serious violation for failing to provide workers with protective hardhats against falling objects.In total, OSHA proposed $380,664 in penalties.The employer has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

entry.title: US Department of Labor awards $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago Grants to promote mine safety, health education
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago grant funding to two organizations to support education and training initiatives that will help identify and prevent unsafe working conditions in and around the nation’s mines.Administered by the department’s Mine Safety and Health Administration, the Brookwood-Sago Mine Safety grant program helps recipients create training materials, conduct mine safety training, and educational programs designed to protect the safety and health of miners. In awarding the grants, MSHA focused on innovative plans for mine safety and pilot programs that may be useful for miners working in a broad range of positions. The grants also put an emphasis on programs and materials targeting workers in smaller mines that train mine operators and miners about MSHA standards, and emergency response training.Established under the Mine Improvement and New Emergency Response Act of 2006, the grant program honors the miners lost at the Jim Walter Resources #5 mine in Brookwood, Alabama, on Sept. 23, 2001, and at the Sago Mine in Buckhannon, West Virginia, on Jan. 2, 2006.The recipients of the 2026 Brookwood-Sago grants are as follows:RecipientCityState/TerritoryAmountSaelua Medical Corporation Pago PagoAmerican Samoa$170,000University of ArizonaTucsonAZ$80,000

entry.title: US Department of Labor finds none of nation’s 12,000 mining operations met criteria for pattern of violations in fiscal year 2026
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Mine Safety and Health Administration announced today that none of the nation’s 12,000 mining operations met the criteria for a pattern of violations notice, one of the agency’s toughest enforcement tools.In MSHA’s annual screening of operations from Oct. 1, 2025, to Sept. 30, 2026, the agency found no pattern of violation notices. The Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977 includes the pattern of violations provision for mines with a recurring pattern of significant and substantial violations – those that are reasonably likely to result in a serious injury or illness – and other safety and health compliance problems. If a mine receives subsequent S&S violations after being placed on POV, MSHA is authorized to withdraw miners from the affected area of the mine.“Under this administration MSHA remains committed to objectively calling balls and strikes in enforcement, including issuing POV notices when warranted,” said Assistant Secretary for Mine Safety and Health Wayne D. Palmer. “For the third year in a row, no mine received a POV notice which, combined with the lowest-ever all-injury rate in 2025, signals continued progress toward protecting miners from safety and health hazards.”MSHA provides mine operators with online tools to help monitor compliance. The POV calculator allows mine operators to monitor performance under the POV screening criteria and alerts mine operators that corrective actions are needed. The agency’s S&S calculator enables mine operators to monitor their “significant and substantial” violations. It is the responsibility of mine operators to track their violation and injury histories to determine whether they need to take action to avoid meeting the POV screening criteria.
